overview: The two vesicle-mediated bulk transport processes cells use to bring material in or send material out.
genZNote: Endocytosis: the cell orders takeout. Exocytosis: it sends the package.

aspects.label: Overview / Core Definition
aspects.valueA: The process by which a cell engulfs material from outside by folding its membrane inward to form a vesicle.
aspects.valueB: The process by which a cell releases material by fusing an internal vesicle with the plasma membrane.

aspects.label: Direction of Movement
aspects.valueB: Out of the cell (intracellular to extracellular).

aspects.label: Vesicle Formation
aspects.valueA: Plasma membrane invaginates around the material, pinching off to form a vesicle.
aspects.valueB: A pre-formed intracellular vesicle travels to and fuses with the plasma membrane.

aspects.label: Subtypes
aspects.valueA: Phagocytosis ("cell eating"), pinocytosis ("cell drinking"), receptor-mediated endocytosis.
aspects.valueB: Constitutive (continuous, unregulated) and regulated (triggered, e.g. by calcium signaling) exocytosis.

aspects.label: Biological Example
aspects.valueA: A macrophage engulfing a bacterium; LDL uptake via receptor-mediated endocytosis.
aspects.valueB: Neurons releasing neurotransmitter into the synaptic cleft; secretion of hormones or digestive enzymes.

aspects.label: Energy Requirement
aspects.valueA: Requires ATP — an active, energy-dependent bulk transport process.
aspects.valueB: Requires ATP — also active and energy-dependent.

aspects.label: Key Distinguishing Feature
aspects.valueA: Membrane folds inward to import material.
aspects.valueB: Vesicle fuses outward to export material.
